title: Pick SOURCE, CLASS or RUNTIME for each annotation

blocks.text: The page's Q1 gives one annotation per retention policy:

items: `@ReviewNeeded(reason)`: a note for people and the compiler. It must **never reach the class file**: SOURCE.
`@GeneratedCode(generator)`: for bytecode tools. It must be **kept in the class file but hidden from reflection**: CLASS, which the page says to state explicitly even though it is the default.
`@Cacheable(cacheName, ttlSeconds)`: read by a framework while the program runs: RUNTIME.

blocks.text: `Retained` declares the three without any `@Retention`, plus the page's `Service` that uses them. Give each the right `@Retention`, then write `cached(Class<?> type)`: one line `"<method> -> <cacheName> (<ttlSeconds>s)"` per method `type` declares with `@Cacheable`, sorted.
The tests also read `Service`'s compiled `.class` file to see which annotations the compiler wrote into it.

cases.says: cached(Service.class) reads @Cacheable at run time: [config -> default (300s), getUsers -> users (600s)].
Service's compiled class file does not mention @ReviewNeeded at all.
@GeneratedCode declares @Retention itself; it is written into Service's class file, yet reflection cannot see it.

concepts: The job decides the policy: SOURCE for compile-time notes, CLASS for bytecode tools, RUNTIME for frameworks that read annotations while the program runs.
isAnnotationPresent, getAnnotation and getAnnotations read RUNTIME annotations on classes, methods and fields.
SOURCE annotations are dropped by the compiler, CLASS annotations are written to the class file but not loaded for reflection, and RUNTIME annotations are also readable by reflection.
